title: Cofinality is invariant under coherent natural equivalence
statement:
Use quasicategories, internal functor categories, coherent natural equivalences, weak contractibility and degreewise simplicial pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $A,B$ be quasicategories in a fixed universe, and let $u,v:A\to B$ be functors joined by a coherent natural equivalence, meaning an equivalence edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(A,B)$. For a vertex $b\in B$ and a functor $w:A\to B$, define the exact arrow-comma simplicial set
$$M_b(w)=\{b\}\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B,w}A.$$
Then $M_b(u)$ is weakly contractible for every $b\in B$ if and only if $M_b(v)$ is weakly contractible for every $b\in B$. The universe may be any one containing $A,B$ and the natural-equivalence data; neither category is required to be small in a previously fixed smaller universe.

source.place: HTT Corollary 4.1.1.10 and Proposition 4.1.1.8, with Theorem 4.1.3.1; mapping-space proof for the exact arrow-comma model extracted from the returned Step 8. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial or quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: Choose nested universes large enough to contain A, B, the functors and the coherent equivalence, and regard A and B as small in the enlarged universe. The displayed pullback M_b(w) is exactly the coherent comma (b↓w) in [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test]. Its equivalence of conditions (3) and (4) says that M_b(w) is weakly contractible for every b if and only if colim_{a∈A} H_B(b,w(a)) is contractible for every b. We use this equivalence of universally quantified conditions, without asserting a pointwise comparison of the two objects. The coherent mapping bifunctor H_B and its source-fixed arrow model are supplied by [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. The containing-universe convention permits this enlargement, and the space test supplies the small space colimits used below.

source.place: HTT Corollary 4.1.1.10 and Proposition 4.1.1.8, with Theorem 4.1.3.1; the mapping-space proof of invariance under a coherent natural equivalence.

proof.text: Let η:u⇒v be the equivalence edge in Fun(A,B). By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences], every component η_a:u(a)→v(a) is an equivalence edge of B. Composing the map A×Δ¹→B representing η with the source-fixed coherent mapping functor H_B(b,−):B→S of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] gives an edge θ of Fun(A,S) between the diagrams a↦H_B(b,u(a)) and a↦H_B(b,v(a)); its component at a is the image H_B(b,η_a), which by the transport classification acts on H_B(b,u(a)) by postcomposition with η_a, including on higher simplices. A simplicial map carries an equivalence edge, together with its two inverse-triangle witnesses, to an equivalence edge, so every component of θ is an equivalence edge of S. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] applied in Fun(A,S), θ is an equivalence edge: the two diagrams are coherently naturally equivalent.

source.place: HTT Corollary 4.1.1.10 and Proposition 4.1.1.8, with Theorem 4.1.3.1; the mapping-space proof of invariance under a coherent natural equivalence.

proof.text: Fix b and denote the diagrams in Step 2 by F and G and their coherent equivalence by θ:F→G. Choose an inverse equivalence edge ρ:G→F with its two inverse-triangle witnesses. Take a colimiting cocone λ:F→Δ_A L in S. Compose to get μ=λρ:G→Δ_A L. For any space T, the dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that Map(L,T)→Map(F,Δ_A T), a↦(Δ_A a)λ, is an equivalence. In the quasicategory Fun(A,S), precomposition with ρ gives Map(F,Δ_A T)→Map(G,Δ_A T); by the associativity and unit homotopies of the canonical composition in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], precomposition with θ is a homotopy inverse, because θρ and ρθ have the identity component classes. The same associativity homotopy identifies the composite Map(L,T)→Map(F,Δ_A T)→Map(G,Δ_A T) up to homotopy with the cocone test a↦(Δ_A a)μ for μ, so that test is an equivalence and μ is colimiting as well. Thus the same space L is the apex of a colimiting cocone on each diagram. Any chosen colimit of G is equivalent to L: both cocones are initial objects of the same cocone category, whose initial-object full subcategory is a contractible Kan complex by the cited calculus, and the apex projection carries the resulting equivalence edge to an equivalence edge of S. Hence the two colimit spaces are equivalent.

source.place: HTT Corollary 4.1.1.10 and Proposition 4.1.1.8, with Theorem 4.1.3.1; the mapping-space proof of invariance under a coherent natural equivalence.

proof.text: Contractibility of a space is invariant under equivalence. By Step 3, for each b the colimit for u is contractible exactly when the colimit for v is contractible. Thus the universally quantified condition (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test] holds for u if and only if it holds for v. Apply the equivalence of conditions (3) and (4) from Step 1 on both sides to conclude the asserted universal weak contractibility of the exact comma simplicial sets.

split_report.summary: Split the extracted natural-equivalence invariance argument into four steps. Apply the cofinality space test with its stated universal quantifier in an enlarged universe, transport the coherent equivalence through the mapping bifunctor, compare colimits by explicit inverse-equivalence precomposition in the cocone criterion, and transfer contractibility. Repaired the earlier pointwise reading of the space test and removed its uncited Yoneda invocation. No new nodes; statement unchanged. Maintainer reader (Q136 review): Step 2 now cites the in-unit lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences for the componentwise criterion; Step 3 cites lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition for the associativity/unit homotopies of precomposition.

tool_uses.why: Step 3 uses its dual cocone mapping-space criterion for colimiting cocones and the contractibility of the full subcategory of initial objects; no node of unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general states these general quasicategory facts.
